source.name: Oslo Offsite — September 2026 (Notion)
source.note: Guide content comes from the Notion invitation. Accommodation listing details, photos and approximate coordinates come from the local guide update dated 9 September 2026. Other coordinates come from Kartverket’s official Norwegian address register (ws.geonorge.no). Walking times are estimates, not measured routes. Entity images come from the local schema 1.4 update; each image records its original source and available credit and licence information.

event.name: Oslo Offsite — September 2026
event.focus: The offsite falls right around the beta release of our SDK, so this time the work will be focused on the SDK.

workingDays.note: Expect to be focused and working on building something we can ship by Friday.

home.name: Christian’s home
home.notes: The home of your local host and one-person support team. Give Christian a call or send a WhatsApp message before dropping by.

places.name: Apostrophe
places.signatureDish: French fries — crisp and perfectly salted

places.name: Render
places.signatureDish: Oslohoma burger — lots of grilled onion and cheese

places.name: Pao
places.signatureDish: Nuggets — tempura-fried chicken thighs with Thai chili, coriander and caramel fish sauce

places.name: Skaal
places.signatureDish: Grilled skewer — Norwegian chuck with miso and prune glaze, mushroom ragù

places.name: Fourrage
places.signatureDish: Steak tartare — coarsely ground flank steak, Caesar dressing, grated Comté

places.name: Bar Lupo
places.signatureDish: Linguine with crab — lots of crab meat and a pangrattato

places.name: Grotto
places.signatureDish: Pistachio ice cream — creamy, nutty, with sweet Italian meringue

places.name: Jamal's Falafel
places.description: Falafel, vegan. Slightly outside the walking zone.

places.name: Rebel Hangout
places.description: Weekday buffet, pay in the cafeteria

places.name: Fuglen
places.description: In Rebel's building, down on the cellar floor. Coffee by day, cocktail bar in the evening, in a preserved 1960s interior. Opened as Kaffefuglen in 1963, renamed Fuglen in 2008.

places.name: Supreme Roastworks
places.description: Odd-Steinar Tøllefsen is World Brewers Cup Champion 2015.

places.name: Java Espressobar & Kaffeforretning
places.description: Opened 1997. Closest of the coffee bars to Rebel.

places.name: Mocca Kaffebar
places.description: Opened 2000. Same company as Java, which also started the KAFFA roastery in 2005.

places.name: Tim Wendelboe
places.description: Espresso bar at Grüners gate 1, roastery at Tøyengata 29c. Norwegian Barista Champion 2001, 2002 and 2004; World Barista Champion 2004; World Cup Tasters Champion 2005.

places.name: Papegøye
places.description: Best hours of the group, useful when working late. In 2022, three of the five baristas on the Norwegian national coffee team were part of the Papegøye family.

places.name: MUNCH
places.description: Art museum. Free on Wednesdays 18:00–21:00, drop-in tickets at the door.
places.priceNote: Free Wed 18:00–21:00, otherwise 200 NOK evening slot, 100 NOK under 25

places.name: Fabrikken Oslo
places.description: Shuffleboard, darts, pool, karaoke, arcade. Bookings: booking@fabrikkenoslo.no
places.priceNote: Whole shuffleboard court 750 NOK/hour, pool 220 NOK/hour, board games free
places.hours: Wed 17:00–01:00, Thu–Sat 16:00–01:00, closed Sun and Mon

places.name: Oslo Camping
places.description: Indoor minigolf, drop-in. Easiest thing to do after a late day.

places.name: Grünerløkka Brygghus
places.description: Own brewery, 21 taps. Walk home to Torshov afterwards.

places.name: Crow Bar & Bryggeri
places.description: Big tap list. Reservations need 6+ people and cannot be same-day.

places.name: Ekebergparken
places.description: Sculpture park in the forest above the city. Tram 13 or 19. Kongsveien is closed for roadworks May–November 2026, so allow an extra 15 minutes and check ruter.no. Sunset around 19:45.

places.name: The National Museum
places.description: Hours taken from VisitOSLO; the museum's own site would not load, so worth a check.

places.name: Good Knight chess pub
places.description: The only chess pub in Oslo.

places.name: Haralds Vaffel
places.description: Heart-shaped Norwegian waffles, soft not crisp.

places.name: Åpent Bakeri
places.description: Cinnamon buns and other Norwegian buns.

places.name: Syverkiosken
places.description: Pølse med lompe — sausage in a potato flatbread. One of the last old wooden kiosks.

places.name: Kiwi Vogts gate
places.description: Nearest supermarket to the Torshov flats.

fromSupermarket.name: Brunost
fromSupermarket.description: Whey cheese boiled until the milk sugar caramelises. Sweet, fudge-like. The item first-time visitors most often dislike. Try it thin, on a waffle.

fromSupermarket.name: Leverpostei
fromSupermarket.description: Baked liver pâté. The default sandwich topping.

fromSupermarket.name: Kaviar
fromSupermarket.description: Smoked cod roe from a tube. Strongly acquired taste.

fromSupermarket.name: Makrell i tomat
fromSupermarket.description: Tinned mackerel in tomato sauce, on bread.

fromSupermarket.name: Solo
fromSupermarket.description: Orange soda, recipe brought from Spain in 1934. Outsold Coca-Cola here in the 1960s.

fromSupermarket.name: Matpakke
fromSupermarket.description: The habit, not a product: bread with the toppings above, wrapped in paper with sheets between the slices. What Norwegians actually eat at work.

outAndAbout.name: Vaffel
outAndAbout.description: Heart-shaped, soft not crisp, with sour cream and jam or brunost.

outAndAbout.name: Fårikål
outAndAbout.description: The national dish. September is the season, but Fårikålens festdag is 24 September, five days after we leave. Restaurant Schrøder or Kaffistova — phone ahead, not confirmed to be on the menu that week.

expoCustomerApps.name: Vy
expoCustomerApps.description: Norway's state-owned national railway. Use it for train travel, not the airport express.

expoCustomerApps.name: Thon Hotels
expoCustomerApps.description: Arriving early and staying at a Thon Hotel? Keep your booking handy, check in and out, and use your phone as your room key.

accommodation.note: All three Torshov Airbnbs are booked and verified. Christian booked them. Private bedrooms for everyone, shared bathrooms. Listing details, photos and coordinates were read from the Airbnb listings on 9 Sept 2026.
accommodation.coordinatePrecisionNote: Airbnb publishes an approximate point, not the street address, so each flat's coordinates are area-accurate to roughly 100-200 m. Exact addresses arrive with the booking confirmations.

options.name: Bright and nice apartment in Torshov
options.hostNote: Two years hosting. Rated 5.0 for communication, responds within an hour.
options.description: Bright apartment on the third floor of a classic building. Master bedroom with a double bed, guest room with a single bed, open kitchen, high ceilings, newly renovated bathroom and a living room. Sleeps three, with a foldable bed for a fourth.
options.neighbourhoodNote: Torshov/Sagene. Walking distance to Grünerløkka, Akerselva and the parks. Public transport nearby, city centre in about 20 minutes.
notes: Some storage in the flat is not for guest use.

options.name: Top apartment in Torshov
options.description: Two floors plus a loft in central Torshov. Two bedrooms with extra sleeping space, an office in the loft, bathroom, laundry room with toilet, living room, kitchen, loft living room and a balcony with good sun. Cosy backyard with grills.
options.neighbourhoodNote: Central Torshov. Bus and light rail two minutes away. Street parking is usually available.
notes: Listing states it is not suitable for children aged 2 to 12.
Host prefers whole-month rentals in July and August, with some flexibility.

photos.caption: Loft sitting area with exposed beams

options.name: Large loft apartment in Torshov
options.description: Large loft apartment on two floors with a view over the city, suited to groups. Fifth floor has the bathroom and four bedrooms, one with a double mattress. Sixth floor is an airy loft with a mezzanine, dining room, sofa group and a well-equipped kitchen.
options.neighbourhoodNote: Torshov, 12 minutes by tram from the city centre. Quiet area with cafes and neighbourhood pubs, close to Grünerløkka and Akerselva.
amenities: HDTV with Disney+, Netflix and HBO Max
notes: Fifth and sixth floor, no lift.
Four bedrooms but a five-guest maximum, so one room is a single.

photos.caption: Dining area beneath the skylight at dusk
Dining table and skylight seating in daylight
Fireplace between the dining area and kitchen

workspace.name: Rebel
workspace.notes: Co-working space in the centre of Oslo. Everyone gets access cards and free wifi. It has a restaurant for lunch.

notes: It can rain a fair bit at this time of year
Ideally with a hood so you don't need an umbrella
Bring one or two, so you can do t-shirt to sweater to raincoat
For the fjord sauna on 15 September

packingNote: Mid-September in Oslo is cool and often wet, so layers and rain protection are the priority. You can pick most things up locally. An umbrella is optional.

faq.question: Do I need cash?
faq.answer: No. Norway is almost entirely cashless — card and Apple/Google Pay work everywhere, and locals mostly use Vipps. Many places won't even accept cash, so there's no need to bring any.

arrival.note: Local Oslo landing time. LH 866 is Lufthansa Frankfurt to Oslo, departing 13 Sept at 22:00. The Notion doc lists this under 13 Sept because that is the departure date. Lufthansa's current published schedule for this route is 22:10 to 00:15, so confirm the exact minutes against Hirbod's ticket.

assets.note: Asset paths are relative to the app project root. All guide images are bundled through the static asset registry.
assets.rightsNote: Every image was downloaded from the source recorded on the entity: usually the venue's or producer's own website, otherwise VisitOSLO, VisitLokka, MerAvOslo, Flickr or the App Store. None is licensed for republication. Fine for an internal team app; clear the rights before using any of them in anything public.
